lines.text: Today the Moon is about half a degree wide, about the width of a small pea held at arm's length.
Now sink it until its surface is four hundred kilometers above ours, the height of the space station.
Straight underneath it, the Moon would be about seventy-eight degrees wide.
The sky from one horizon to the other is a hundred eighty degrees.
So one Moon would stretch across nearly half of it.
That's about one hundred fifty times wider than the Moon you know.
And it would not sit still. So which way would it cross the sky, and how fast?
The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
